title: Modulation of Therapeutic Response in Lung Cancer by Tumor Suppressor LKB1
text:
Lung cancer characterized by LKB1 deficiency is common, notably aggressive, and typically resistant to
existing therapies. This study aims to understand and target a previously unrecognized mechanism underlying
the aggressiveness and treatment resistance associated with LKB1 deficiency. It will establish proof-of-concept
for innovative therapeutic strategies targeting LKB1-mutated lung cancer.

title: Enhancing the antitumor effect of radiation therapy by targeting the cGAS-STING pathway
text:
Metastasis is responsible for about 2/3 of cancer deaths. This proposal aims to improve the treatment outcome
of metastatic cancer by enhancing the antitumor effect of radiation therapy through combination with agents that
stimulate the host’s innate immunity. Completion of this project will open new possibilities of cancer
immunotherapy to treat metastatic cancers.

title: Core C: Biostatistical and Bioinformatics Core
text: The development and application of new computational methodology for cancer research has expanded roles for statisticians and computational experts. The Biostatistics and Bioinformatics Core provides the statistical, bioinformatics, and computational support for all SPORE in Pancreatic Cancer investigators. Core C will support consultation and collaboration on all aspects of study design, database development and quality control, and data analysis, interpretation, and presentation of data.

title: Novel Mechanisms underlying abdominal aortic aneurysm progression
text:
Abdominal aortic aneurysm (AAA) is a potentially lethal disease that lacks pharmacological treatment, and aortic
wall medial smooth muscle degeneration and adventitia remodeling are the determining factors for AAA
progression and aortic rupture. In this application, a combination of molecular, cellular, and genetic approaches
with gain-of- and loss-of-function studies will be used to establish novel mechanisms by which Smad2 hinders
AAA progression by inhibiting vascular smooth muscle necroptosis while facilitating adventitia protective
responses. The outcome of the project may lead to the development of new strategies for the prevention or
therapy of AAA.

title: Cell-drones: engineered stem cell nanovesicles as alternatives to exosomes
text:
Extracellular vesicle (EV) therapy is a promising strategy for tissue regeneration. But the large-scale production
of EVs remains a challenge. In the proposed study, we seek to develop a scale-up friendly method to generate
a large number of therapeutic nanovesicles (NV) from MSCs by extrusion.

title: A Personalized Digital Intervention to Reduce Alcohol Use and Improve HIV Care Outcomes
text:
Hazardous alcohol use and negative affect (e.g., anxiety and depression) are common among people with HIV and
worsen health outcomes, including medication adherence and quality of life. There is a pressing need to develop
scalable, low-cost interventions that address both hazardous drinking and negative affect among persons with HIV
to improve HIV care in line with PAS-25-208’s emphasis on scalable, cross-cutting interventions that reduce
differences in health outcomes and improve engagement in HIV care. The proposed R01 study will address this
major public health priority as we propose to develop and test the efficacy of a brief, integrated, single-session,
personalized feedback intervention, designed to address co-occurring hazardous drinking and elevated negative
affect symptoms among persons with HIV.

title: Genetic resiliency to disease progression in Alzheimer's disease
text:
A subset of individuals exhibits resilience to Alzheimer’s disease, as indicated by significant Alzheimer’s disease
neuropathology on autopsy despite intact cognition. Underlying pathways that engage this resilience remain
largely unknown, making it difficult to develop targeted therapies that harness these naturally-occurring
pathways. My goal is to investigate genetic mechanisms of natural resilience, so that we can design strategies
that leverage these underlying mechanisms to therapeutically confer resilience to Alzheimer’s disease
progression.

title: From genetic association to function: pleiotropic novel genes and variants linking lipid metabolism and cardiovascular diseases
text:
The proposed research program utilizes a systematic approach to investigate new genetic discoveries associated with
blood lipids and cardiovascular disease (CVD). The investigators aim to demonstrate this through a paradigm of
functional characterization of newly discovered lipid-regulating genes using naturally-occurring genetic variants. This
effort will help bridge the significant gaps in knowledge linking human genomic discoveries to new biology and
therapeutic targets and provide a roadmap for how novel genomic loci, genes, and variants associated with blood lipids
and CVD might be investigated in a systematic manner.

title: The molecular epidemiology of enteropathogenic (EPEC) and enteroaggregative (EAEC) Escherichia coli among adult patients in Seattle
text:
Multiplex molecular panels have facilitated the diagnosis of patients presenting with acute
diarrhea and enabled the rapid detection of diarrheagenic E. coli which were previously
overlooked by conventional clinical laboratory methods. Enteropathogenic (EPEC) and
enteroaggregative (EAEC) E. coli are now among the most common pathogens detected by these
panels. Yet, although both are established as causes of diarrhea in infants living in developing
countries, little is known about their clinical relevance in adult patients living in high-income
countries. The proposed research will examine the clinical features, epidemiology, and
antimicrobial resistance of EPEC/EAEC infections in U.S. adults to better understand their
importance and to inform strategies for their prevention and management.

title: Investigating GLI transcription factors as regulators of the pancreatic cancer microenvironment
text:
Pancreatic cancer is a deadly malignancy, with poor prognosis for patients at all stages of diagnosis. In this
proposal, we will investigate novel roles for GLI transcription factors, the effectors of the Hedgehog signaling
pathway, as key regulators of the pancreatic cancer microenvironment. Specifically, we will: 1) employ novel
genetic approaches to assess the contribution of GLI transcription factors to pancreatic cancer progression, 2)
elucidate GLI-dependent fibroblast-immune crosstalk and 3) define GLI transcriptional targets in pancreatic
fibroblasts to positively impact the treatment of pancreatic cancer.

title: Multimodal machine learning for diagnosis and mechanistic phenotyping of inherited diseases
text:
Rare genetic diseases collectively affect 300 million individuals worldwide, yet many patients experience 
prolonged diagnostic delays and limited understanding of the biological mechanisms underlying their 
conditions. This project will develop multimodal artificial intelligence tools that combine facial images, clinical 
features, and genomic information to improve diagnostic accuracy, uncover disease mechanisms, and 
ultimately support more timely diagnoses and precision medicine approaches for affected patients.

title: WY INBRE-5 Data Science Core
text: The long-term goal of the Data Science Core (DSC) is to develop a robust biomedical data science infrastructure (education, analysis, collaboration) that continues to increase the research productivity of Wyoming researchers and provides career-enhancing training for Wyoming students. The primary goal of the DSC during INBRE 4 was to build on successful data science programs supported by previous INBRE funding with a plan that acknowledges the state’s needs and considers the unique structure of its INBRE network. The DSC will pursue the following three objectives to achieve this DSC-specific goal, as well as the overall Specific Aims in Wyoming INBRE 5: 1. Support research computing and data science expertise at the University of Wyoming (UW) by enhancing and extending successful INBRE-4 programs. 2. Foster development of data science skills at community colleges (CCs) and state entities. 3. Expand the impact of the DSC’s work through continued engagement with regional and national INBRE programs and their networks. The expected outcomes of the DSC include successful educational and collaborative data science research projects, which at the UW will generate publications in the peer-reviewed literature and at the CCs will provide student exposure to high performance computing, cloud computing, and data science methodologies. Data science training will continue to support the transition to independent analyses for research groups. Tangible resources in the form of sample preparation and sequencing instrumentation, awards for data generation and travel grants to acquire specialized training, will position Network investigators to compete successfully for external funding. DSC staff will also continue the development of the burgeoning UW/CC undergraduate curriculum in computational biology and through teaching of dedicated short courses. Outcomes of work with state entities will include continued support in data analysis, training, and expanding the internship program to improve workforce development. These project outcomes will positively impact the Network's ability to use data science approaches in their research and on career trajectories and workforce development for student and state entity trainees. We believe that our new permanent research training lab, our dedicated network computing environment, and new faculty affiliate in Casper will enhance the DSC’s ability to support community college and UW faculty to add bioinformatics modules into existing courses.

title: Histone demethylase control of primordial germ cell specification
text:
Primordial germ cells (PGCs), the precursors to sperm and egg, undergo global epigenetic remodeling
including erasure of repressive histone modifications, such as H3K9me2 and DNA methylation. Improper
retention of these epigenetic modifications could compromise germ cell development and lead to
transgenerational epigenetic inheritance. In this proposal I will investigate how the H3K9me2 demethylases,
KDM3A and KDM3B, regulate epigenetic remodeling in PGCs, which has important implications for reproductive
biology and medicine.

title: Synaptic Organization and Modulation of Kainate Receptors: Investigating the Structure, Dynamics, and Function in the Context of Trans-Synaptic Junctions
text:
Kainate receptors are ionotropic glutamate receptors important in synapse regulation and have been linked to
neurological deficits including epilepsy, autism, mental retardation, and schizophrenia, making them important
as pharmacological targets. Postsynaptic kainate receptors have been found to create a trans-synaptic junction
with presynaptic Neurexin3β and extracellular scaffolding C1q-like protein as an intermediate. This proposal
aims to investigate the functional and structural properties of this junction in order to understand the role this
trans-synaptic junction plays in neuron function and correlate this junction with known behavioral deficits.

title: Stanford Molecular Imaging Scholars (SMIS) Program
text:
RELEVANCE TO PUBLIC HEALTH
The Stanford Molecular Imaging Scholars (SMIS) program is a unique, integrated, and cross-
disciplinary postdoctoral training program that prepares young investigators for research careers
in the field of molecular imaging of cancer. Molecular imaging explores and creates new
approaches to visualize and quantify specific molecular and biochemical processes in intact living
organisms and provides especially powerful tools for the study of cancer. SMIS trainees develop
innovative molecular imaging approaches for the diagnosis and management of cancer, including
the development of novel probes, instruments, and assays to characterize as well as guide the
selection and/or discovery of novel treatments, and the evaluation of therapy response.

title: Stories to Prevent (StoP) HPV Cancers: A communication intervention to increase HPV cancer prevention in primary care
text: The proposed study, Stories to Prevent (StoP) HPV Cancers, evaluates the association of a narrative communication intervention delivered through digital and mobile technologies before wellness visits on initiation of HPV cancer prevention services among children ages 9-12. The project is relevant to public health because it aims to reduce HPV-associated cancers by addressing parents’ communication needs with an intervention that fits the technology ecosystem and workflow of primary care clinics. The project is relevant to the National Cancer Institute because it aims to demonstrate the efficacy of a highly scalable communication intervention to educate, engage, and encourage parents to get a cancer-preventing service for their children.

title: Cortical mechanisms of opioid reinforcement
text:
How opioids act in the brain to drive opioid use disorder (OUD) is poorly understood. We recently identified a
population of cortical pyramidal neurons that express μ opioid receptors (μORs) and project to the parabrachial
nucleus (PBn). μOR-mediated inhibition of these cortical neurons was necessary for opioids to elicit their
rewarding effects. Here, we will use a cutting-edge multidisciplinary approach to define the role of these newly
identified cortical neurons in regulating the motivational properties of opioids that contribute to OUD. This
program of research promises to yield important new insights into the mechanisms of OUD.

title: Death receptor signaling as an immune checkpoint in tumor-specific iPSC-T cell function
text:
Engineered T cell therapies for cancer have demonstrated the potential to treat cancers otherwise unresponsive
to existing treatments, however, solving barriers to access and expanding the number of cancer types responsive
to T cell therapies requires new innovations. This project seeks to develop the potential of pluripotent stem cell-
derived T cells (PSC-T) as an effective and readily available source of T cells for future cell therapies through
studying a way to enhance their therapeutic efficacy against tumor cells.

title: Elucidating and bypassing molecular mechanisms that suppress Muller glia-dependent regeneration of cones in two zebrafish models of chronic retinal damage
text:
Vision loss is among the top ten disabilities in the United States, with an estimated burden on society of over
$35 billion and approximately 285 million people worldwide being visually impaired and 39 million being blind.
Many of the causes of vision loss are slow and chronic. We will examine why zebrafish regenerate retinal
neurons following a rapid acute damage, but not a slow chronic damage, which may result in the development
of novel therapies to restore vision to humans who suffer from chronic retinal degenerative diseases.

title: Pbx-Directed Control of Cellular Behaviors that Drive Midface Morphogenesis
text:
Cleft lip with or without cleft palate (CL/P) represents the most common craniofacial birth defect and is a
burden for the individual and society. We will investigate the cell behaviors, genetic pathways, and regulatory
networks underlying facial prominence fusion to identify new genes for prenatal diagnostics and tissue repair
of CL/P.
